text: agent1 (db) report: db logs show FATAL 'too many clients' — max_connections=20, 20/20 in use, 113 connection attempts rejected in last minute. Peak concurrent demand from app pools over last hour: 90. So db is saturated by app-side connection demand (~90 vs 20 limit). Likely cause is app connection pool size/leak (agent2's area), not db itself. Proposal: agent2 should be incident commander since root cause appears in app pools. I will NOT run remediation. Please confirm what app pool config you see, and agent3 please check whether LB is retrying/amplifying traffic.

agent2 (app) here. App logs show repeated 'timeout acquiring DB connection from pool (waited 5000 ms)' from OrderService, plus slow health checks. This points to DB connection exhaustion or slow DB, not an app code fault I can see. Status: order error rate 38%, p99 9.2s. I have not run any remediation. @agent1 can you check DB connection count / slow queries? @agent3 can you check whether LB traffic volume or retries spiked? Proposal: whoever owns the root cause commands remediation.

agent3 (lb): lb logs show 'primary route ok, packet loss 0.0%'. No LB-side fault visible. Status: DEGRADED, 38% errors, p99 9.2s. agent1/agent2: please post your db/app log findings. I will not run remediation until root cause is located; whoever owns the root cause area should be commander.

agent1 (db): Summary. DB is at its hard limit (max_connections=20, 20/20 used, 113 rejects/min). Demand from app pools peaked at 90 in the last hour, and agent2 sees pool acquire timeouts, so the connection flood comes from the app side. Root cause = app connection demand exceeding DB limit; I have no DB-side fault (no slow-query or disk logs visible to me). Proposal: agent2 is incident commander. Suggested app-side fix: cap pool size per instance so total stays under 20 (or fewer after scale). I will not change DB config unless agent2 asks for it, since raising max_connections is untested and could add memory pressure. I'm standing by to verify DB connection count after the change.

agent3 (lb): Agree with agent1. LB is not the cause (route ok, 0% loss). Agent2 should be incident commander. I will not run remediation. I can check LB retry or connection behavior if the app-side pool cap changes the traffic pattern; tell me if you want that.

agent2 (app): I accept incident commander since the root cause is app-side connection demand. Plan: (1) confirm current app pool config and instance count, (2) cap per-instance pool so total stays under 20 DB connections, (3) do not scale app up, since more instances means more connections. agent1: please keep DB config unchanged and tell me the connection count after each change. agent3: please keep watching LB retries so they don't amplify load.
agent3 (lb): Acknowledged. Watching LB retries. Current LB log: primary route ok, 0% loss. I will report any retry amplification right away.

agent2 (commander): I could not find the app pool-size config key. Guessed names (db_pool_max_size, db_pool_size, pool_size, max_pool_size) all returned 'no effect', so nothing was changed. Next I will restart the app tier to clear its pooled connections and see whether DB connections drop and errors fall. agent1: please report DB connection count right after the restart. agent3: please watch for retry spikes during the restart.
agent1 (db): Acknowledged, agent2 as commander. Restart of app tier is reasonable. I will report DB connection count and rejects immediately after the restart.

agent2 (commander) REPORT: my app restart was a mistake. It triggered a reconnection storm and the DB stopped responding. Status is now CRITICAL: order API down (db unreachable). I will not run any more remediation until we agree on a plan. agent1: is the DB process still up? Can you check connection count and whether it needs a restart, and what you recommend? Please do not restart the DB without telling me first. Proposal: once DB is up, we bring app up with a small pool cap, and only one instance at a time.

agent3 (lb): Status is CRITICAL. LB is still healthy (route ok, 0% loss) and is NOT the cause of the DB outage. Recommendation for agent2 (commander): before bringing the app back, keep traffic off the app tier so the reconnection storm does not repeat. Options: (a) if the LB supports a drain/shed or rate-limit setting, apply it so no new orders reach the app until the pool cap is in place; (b) bring app back as one instance, with one reconnect path, and confirm DB connections stay under 20 before adding more. I do NOT recommend failover lb: the LB is not the fault, and a failover would add risk. agent1: please confirm whether the DB process is up. I will not run any remediation unless agent2 asks me to.

agent1 (db) to agent2 (commander): DB log now says 'database not responding (crashed after connection storm)'. I can't see a DB process-level status from my side beyond that line, so I'll treat it as down. Recommendation, agreeing with your plan: (1) you run 'ops.py restart db' once, with max_connections left at 20 (do not raise it during recovery). (2) Wait ~60s and check DB logs for 'ready' and connection count near 0. (3) Bring app up with a small pool cap, one instance at a time, using set-config or scale app 1 if available. (4) Watch DB connections after each step; if they climb toward 20 again, stop and scale app back down. I will run no remediation myself. Please confirm before you restart the DB.

agent2 (commander): I am scaling app to 0 instances now, so no app connections are made while the DB recovers. Next step, as agent1 proposed: one 'restart db' with max_connections=20 unchanged. agent1, I am going ahead with that restart now. Please confirm DB log says 'ready' and report connection count. Then I will bring app up as 1 instance with a pool cap.

agent2 (commander): DB restarted once (max_connections unchanged at 20). Status is DEGRADED again (38% errors), app is at 0 instances. agent1: please report DB connection count and whether DB is ready. Please do not change DB config.

agent3 (lb): Status is DEGRADED at 38% errors with app at 0 instances. My LB log still shows 'primary route ok', so the LB is forwarding but has no backend to answer, which may be the source of these errors. Note for agent2: the 38% may be stale or may come from requests that reach a dead app tier. Please confirm whether app=0 means the LB has no healthy backend. I have no LB action to recommend yet; I'm waiting for agent1's DB ready/connection count before we bring app back as 1 instance.

agent1 (db) to agent2: DB is back up, but logs still show 'too many clients, 20/20 in use, 113 rejects in last minute', even with app at 0 instances. Either the restart didn't clear the connections, or the log is stale. Either way, DO NOT bring the app up yet. The app should only come back when DB connections are clearly below the cap. I have no command to kill connections, so I'm checking the log again to see whether the count is falling. If it stays at 20/20 with app at 0, we have connections held by something other than the app (lb or stale sessions), and we should decide next steps together.

agent3 (lb): My LB log shows only 'primary route ok, packet loss 0.0%' with no connection counts, pool info, or client IPs. So I cannot confirm or rule out LB-held connections. agent1: if the DB log can show client source addresses, check whether the 20 connections come from the LB address or from app addresses. That tells us whether the LB is holding connections. I will not change any LB setting without agent2's approval.

agent1 (db): Re agent3's question: the DB log has no client source addresses, pool names, or per-client connection breakdown, so I can't tell whether the 20 connections come from the LB or from app. Latest DB log (after restart, app at 0): still 20/20 in use and 113 rejects/min. Nothing in my tools can kill connections or show session details. Recommendation: keep app at 0 until DB shows connections under the cap. Agent2, please decide the next step; I'd suggest waiting one more check, and if it stays 20/20, escalating before any further restart.

agent2 (commander): Status is DEGRADED (38% errors, p99 9.2s) with app at 0 instances. DB still reports 20/20 connections in use with app down, so the connections are held by something I cannot see or kill. I am stopping remediation now. No further restarts, scaling, or config changes without a new decision. Escalating to the human operator for direction. agent1 and agent3: please hold, and tell me if the DB connection count changes.

agent3 (lb): Standing by. Current state: DEGRADED, DB 20/20 with app at 0, and I see no LB-side fault (route ok, 0% loss, no connection data in my logs). I have no remediation to suggest right now. agent2 (commander): please decide the next step on the DB connection count. If the 20 connections are not from app, the holder is outside app, and we should escalate rather than restart again. I will not run any LB command unless you ask.
